symptoms: Global route overflow report shows >5-10% overflow concentrated in 1-2 regions while average overflow is low
Detail-route completion stalls with remaining vias/shorts clustered in the same GCells as the overflow hotspots
Congestion map heat is co-located with high cell density or many high-pin cells rather than uniform
Wirelength histogram has a long tail of nets with >2x expected length only inside the congested bins

candidate_causes.cause: Floorplan macro placement creating narrow channels or pin-access walls
candidate_causes.distinguishing_check: Overlay congestion map on floorplan; if overflow tracks the edges of large hard macros or narrow corridors between them, and removing/moving one macro drops local overflow >50%, it is floorplan-limited
candidate_causes.typical_fix: Repack macros with larger keep-out or channel spacing; re-floorplan

candidate_causes.cause: Cell density or high-fanout nets forced into a small area by placement constraints
candidate_causes.distinguishing_check: Density report vs congestion; if peak density >70-80% coincides with overflow and a density-aware re-placement (or temporary density screen) clears most overflow, density is primary
candidate_causes.typical_fix: Add density screens, spread high-pin cells, or relax placement blockages

candidate_causes.cause: Insufficient routing tracks / layer assignment (too many nets forced to lower layers)
candidate_causes.distinguishing_check: Layer-usage histogram; if M1-M3 utilization is near 100% while upper layers are sparse in the same region, force more nets upward or add layer preferences
candidate_causes.typical_fix: Adjust layer directives or increase preferred-direction track availability

candidate_causes.cause: Power-grid or blockage over-subscription of routing resources
candidate_causes.distinguishing_check: Compare congestion with power-stripe map; if overflow sits exactly under wide straps or dense via arrays and a temporary power-grid thin-out reduces overflow, PG is the limiter
candidate_causes.typical_fix: Thin or redistribute power straps / via arrays in the hotspot

candidate_causes.cause: Clock-tree or scan-chain routing already consuming tracks before signal route
candidate_causes.distinguishing_check: Route only non-clock nets first; if congestion collapses dramatically, clock/scan pre-routes are the culprit
candidate_causes.typical_fix: Re-route CTS with tighter track budgeting or move clock spines

ordering_rationale: Cheapest visual overlays (floorplan + density + layer usage) first; only then expensive re-placement or power-grid surgery.
classic_trap: Treating global overflow percentage as the primary metric and adding more effort or more layers when the real problem is a single floorplan channel that a 10-minute macro move would fix.

symptoms: Setup slack report shows negative slack on paths whose endpoint is a capture flip-flop with data-path delay >> clock-path delay
Failing endpoints share a common high-fanout net or a long net that appears in many critical paths
WNS is large but TNS is small (few paths) vs both large (systemic)
After incremental timing update, the same cell or net remains on the critical path while surrounding logic moves

candidate_causes.cause: Long net / high RC delay on a critical data path
candidate_causes.distinguishing_check: Path report with net delays broken out; if one or two nets account for >30-40% of data-path delay and their length or via count is anomalous, buffer/size that net
candidate_causes.typical_fix: Insert buffers or upsize drivers on the long net; re-route with higher layer preference

candidate_causes.cause: Insufficient drive strength or cell sizing on combinational path
candidate_causes.distinguishing_check: Cell delay vs load capacitance; if a cell is driving >3-4x its library target load and is on the critical path, sizing it up improves slack without changing topology
candidate_causes.typical_fix: Upsize the weak cells or insert intermediate buffers

candidate_causes.cause: Clock skew or latency imbalance making the capture edge arrive early relative to launch
candidate_causes.distinguishing_check: Compare launch vs capture clock path delays on the failing paths; if capture latency is systematically lower by the amount of the slack deficit, CTS adjustment is required
candidate_causes.typical_fix: Useful-skew CTS or local clock buffer insertion to delay capture

candidate_causes.cause: High-fanout net without adequate buffering (including scan or reset)
candidate_causes.distinguishing_check: Fanout and transition-time report; if a net with fanout >20-30 appears in multiple failing paths and has slow transition, isolate it by temporary idealization
candidate_causes.typical_fix: Rebuild the high-fanout tree with proper buffering

candidate_causes.cause: False or multi-cycle path not constrained, or incorrect derate/OCV applied
candidate_causes.distinguishing_check: Check SDC for the path; if the path is known multi-cycle or false and is being timed as single-cycle, or if derate is applied twice, the failure is constraint-related
candidate_causes.typical_fix: Add false/multi-cycle exceptions or correct derate settings

candidate_causes.cause: Placement of critical path cells far apart after legalization or congestion-driven moves
candidate_causes.distinguishing_check: Physical path length vs logical depth; if cells that should be adjacent are separated by >10-20 sites and a targeted re-place of the path recovers slack, placement is the cause
candidate_causes.typical_fix: Path-based placement or ECO re-place of the critical cone

ordering_rationale: Highest-probability and cheapest (net delay, sizing, constraint) first; clock skew and placement only after data-path is clean.
classic_trap: Blaming the clock tree for every setup failure when the real problem is a single long data net or an unconstrained false path; engineers then over-constrain CTS and create hold problems.

symptoms: Hold slack report shows negative slack on short paths (often launch-capture of the same or adjacent flops) with data-path delay << clock-path delay difference
Failures appear predominantly at min-corner / fast process while setup is clean at max-corner
Many hold violations share a common clock-gating or local clock buffer that has large insertion delay variation
Hold violations concentrate near clock-tree leaves or after recent CTS ECO

candidate_causes.cause: Insufficient hold buffering / delay cells on short data paths
candidate_causes.distinguishing_check: Path report: if data-path cell count is 0-2 and total data delay is smaller than the hold requirement + skew, the path simply needs delay cells
candidate_causes.typical_fix: Insert hold buffers or delay cells on the short paths (ECO)

candidate_causes.cause: Clock skew that makes launch edge arrive late relative to capture (or capture early)
candidate_causes.distinguishing_check: Launch vs capture latency difference on the violating paths; if the skew alone exceeds the data-path delay, CTS rebalancing or useful skew is needed
candidate_causes.typical_fix: CTS re-optimization for hold or local clock delay insertion on launch

candidate_causes.cause: OCV / derate / CRPR settings too pessimistic (or missing CRPR)
candidate_causes.distinguishing_check: Re-run hold analysis with CRPR enabled or with reduced derate; if violations disappear, the margin stack-up was artificial
candidate_causes.typical_fix: Enable CRPR, tune derate, or use AOCV/POCV tables appropriate to the node

candidate_causes.cause: Min-delay cell library characterization or operating-condition mismatch
candidate_causes.distinguishing_check: Compare reported cell delays against SPICE or library datasheet at the same corner; if library min-delay is unrealistically small, library or corner definition is wrong
candidate_causes.typical_fix: Correct library or operating-condition setup

candidate_causes.cause: Clock-gating cell or integrated clock-gating (ICG) placement creating large local skew
candidate_causes.distinguishing_check: If all hold fails share one ICG and moving/re-buffering that ICG removes the cluster, the ICG is the source
candidate_causes.typical_fix: Re-place or re-buffer the offending ICG; add delay on the short data side

ordering_rationale: Cheapest data-path delay insertion and constraint/derate checks first; only then CTS surgery, because hold ECOs are far cheaper than re-CTS.
classic_trap: Inserting large numbers of hold buffers that later create setup problems or congestion, when a modest CTS skew adjustment or correct CRPR would have fixed most of the violations.

symptoms: Static IR map shows voltage drop >5-10% of Vdd in localized regions while average drop is acceptable
Dynamic IR (or vector-based) peaks coincide with simultaneous switching of large clock or bus domains
IR hotspots sit under high-activity blocks or under sparse power-grid areas
Timing paths that pass through the IR hotspot show extra delay only when IR is annotated

candidate_causes.cause: Insufficient power-grid density or missing straps/via arrays in the hotspot
candidate_causes.distinguishing_check: Overlay IR map on power-grid density; if the hotspot has measurably lower metal/via density and adding a local strap or via farm reduces drop proportionally, grid density is the cause
candidate_causes.typical_fix: Add or widen power straps / increase via density in the region

candidate_causes.cause: High simultaneous switching (clock or large data bus) without local decoupling
candidate_causes.distinguishing_check: Dynamic IR with activity vectors; if peaks align with clock edges or a specific bus toggle and adding decap cells under the block cuts the peak, activity + missing decap is the issue
candidate_causes.typical_fix: Insert decap cells or reduce simultaneous switching (clock gating, staggered enables)

candidate_causes.cause: Package / bump / C4 or power-pad placement creating long resistive paths
candidate_causes.distinguishing_check: IR from pad/bump to the hotspot; if the majority of the drop is between the package pin and the die edge, package or pad placement is limiting
candidate_causes.typical_fix: Add more power pads/bumps or re-assign package pins closer to the hotspot

candidate_causes.cause: Instance-level current draw higher than expected (wrong activity or library power)
candidate_causes.distinguishing_check: Compare instance current vs power report; if a few cells show current far above library expectation under the same vector, activity factor or power characterization is wrong
candidate_causes.typical_fix: Correct activity annotation or replace anomalous cells

candidate_causes.cause: Via resistance or electromigration-limited via arrays under-sized
candidate_causes.distinguishing_check: Via current density report co-located with IR hotspot; if vias are at or above EM limit and increasing via count reduces both EM and IR, via sizing is the cause (more critical at advanced nodes)
candidate_causes.typical_fix: Increase via multiplicity or widen via arrays

ordering_rationale: Local grid density and decap checks are fastest to confirm and cheapest to fix; package and activity annotation come later because they require more data or longer turn-around.
classic_trap: Adding blanket decap everywhere when the real problem is a missing power strap or sparse via array under one block; the extra decap then hurts congestion and area without solving the root IR path.

symptoms: Clock latency or skew report shows global skew > target (often >50-100 ps) or local skew outliers on specific leaves
Clock-tree depth or buffer count is unusually high in one region while other regions are shallow
Setup/hold failures appear only after CTS and disappear when clocks are idealized
Clock transition times at leaves exceed library limits or show large variation across corners

candidate_causes.cause: Unbalanced clock-tree topology or uneven sink distribution
candidate_causes.distinguishing_check: Clock-tree structure browser or latency histogram by region; if one cluster of sinks has 2-3 more buffer levels than the average, re-clustering or forced balancing is needed
candidate_causes.typical_fix: Re-run CTS with tighter skew target or explicit balance constraints on the outlier cluster

candidate_causes.cause: Clock-gating cells or ICGs inserted too deep or with poor placement
candidate_causes.distinguishing_check: If latency jumps occur exactly at ICG boundaries and moving the ICG closer to the root or leaves removes the jump, ICG placement is the cause
candidate_causes.typical_fix: Re-place ICGs closer to the center of their fanout or promote gating higher in the tree

candidate_causes.cause: Routing blockage or congestion forcing long detours on clock nets
candidate_causes.distinguishing_check: Clock net length vs Manhattan; if actual routed length is >> Manhattan in a region that also has signal congestion, the clock is detouring
candidate_causes.typical_fix: Reserve clock routing tracks or move blockages; re-route clock with higher priority

candidate_causes.cause: Incorrect clock uncertainty, latency target, or leaf-pin capacitance annotation
candidate_causes.distinguishing_check: Compare CTS input constraints vs actual leaf capacitance and required uncertainty; if the tool was given wrong leaf C or too aggressive skew, the tree is over-built
candidate_causes.typical_fix: Correct SDC / capacitance annotation and re-CTS

candidate_causes.cause: OCV / AOCV derates making the tool build an overly conservative tree
candidate_causes.distinguishing_check: Re-CTS with reduced derate or with CRPR-aware mode; if skew and buffer count drop substantially while still meeting real silicon margin, derate was excessive (especially visible at advanced nodes with large AOCV tables)
candidate_causes.typical_fix: Tune AOCV/POCV tables or enable advanced OCV modes

ordering_rationale: Constraint and topology visual checks first (minutes); only then re-CTS or blockage surgery, because a full CTS re-run is expensive.
classic_trap: Re-running CTS with ever-tighter skew targets when the real problem is a single misplaced ICG or a routing blockage; the tighter target then explodes buffer count and creates new IR and congestion issues.

symptoms: DRC report shows remaining shorts, spacing, or via violations after detail route, concentrated in previously congested GCells
Same net or same via array appears in many DRC markers (systematic) vs random isolated markers
Violations appear only after metal-fill or after a late ECO that added cells/wires
Minimum-area or enclosure violations dominate rather than pure spacing/shorts

candidate_causes.cause: Residual congestion that detail router could not resolve
candidate_causes.distinguishing_check: Overlay final DRC markers on the last congestion map; if >70% of shorts/spacing sit inside the top-10 overflow GCells, congestion is still the root
candidate_causes.typical_fix: Reduce local density or open more routing tracks, then re-detail-route

candidate_causes.cause: Via or cut-layer rules (enclosure, spacing, min-area) violated by automatic via insertion
candidate_causes.distinguishing_check: Filter DRC by via/cut type; if the majority are enclosure or min-area on a specific via definition, force via pillars or change via selection rules
candidate_causes.typical_fix: Update via rules or insert multi-cut vias / via pillars (critical at advanced nodes)

candidate_causes.cause: Metal-fill or dummy-fill creating new spacing or density violations
candidate_causes.distinguishing_check: Compare DRC before vs after fill; if new markers appear only on fill shapes or at fill-to-signal interfaces, fill rules need adjustment
candidate_causes.typical_fix: Re-run fill with larger keep-out or density-aware constraints

candidate_causes.cause: ECO or late cell insertion that ignored existing routes
candidate_causes.distinguishing_check: If DRC markers sit exactly on the new ECO cells or their newly created pins, and the rest of the design is clean, the ECO is the source
candidate_causes.typical_fix: ECO re-route of the affected nets or legalize the new cells with proper spacing

candidate_causes.cause: Incorrect or incomplete technology LEF / rule deck (missing or wrong spacing tables)
candidate_causes.distinguishing_check: Same geometry passes in a reference deck or in a pure geometric check but fails in the sign-off deck; or identical patterns elsewhere in the design are clean
candidate_causes.typical_fix: Correct the rule deck or LEF and re-verify

candidate_causes.cause: Antenna or end-of-line rules triggered by long dangling wires or missing diodes
candidate_causes.distinguishing_check: Antenna report co-located with DRC markers of antenna type; if adding antenna diodes or breaking the long wire clears them, antenna is the cause
candidate_causes.typical_fix: Insert antenna diodes or jumpers; re-route the offending nets

ordering_rationale: Congestion overlay and via-type filtering are cheapest and highest-probability; technology-deck and antenna checks come later because they are less common once the design is mature.
classic_trap: Running endless detail-route iterations or 'fix-DRC' scripts when the underlying problem is still global congestion; the router keeps producing the same shorts because there is simply no space.
